title: Human Poverty Index
definition: The Human Poverty Index (HPI) is a composite index introduced by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in 1997 in its Human Development Report to measure the deprivation in the basic dimensions of human development in developing (HPI-1) and developed (HPI-2) countries.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial microtopic under UPSC GS Paper III (Economy - Inclusive Growth, Poverty, Human Development) and GS Paper I (Social Issues). Essential for understanding alternative paradigms of poverty measurement beyond mere income deprivation.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Human Poverty Index.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic concepts of Human Development Index (HDI)
